picks.style: latin orphic lament, single lyre and low bowed drone, high plaintive voice, slow, spellbound, suspended
picks.why: Orpheus stops the rivers and the beasts, and the Moon reins in her horses to listen — and it still is not enough.

picks.style: latin underworld song, hollow flute and dark strings, thin spectral voice, slow, hushed, reproachful
picks.why: The ghost of the gnat wakes the shepherd to accuse him: 'I am driven, the prey of Charon.'

picks.style: roman pastoral farewell, reed pipe and soft lyre, warm baritone, unhurried, tender, fading
picks.why: The parting line is a small perfect blessing: 'I depart, never to return. You, tend the spring and the green woods.'

picks.style: georgian pastoral ode, baroque strings and flute, warm tenor, flowing, bright, welcoming
picks.why: 'Come, gentle Spring, aethereal mildness, come' — an invocation built to be sung, with Winter walking off north behind it.

picks.style: spenserian song of temptation, harp and viol, low seductive voice, languid, drowsy, hypnotic
picks.why: The enchanter's call from the Castle of Indolence — 'O come, ye weary Wights, to me!' — a refrain with a hook already in it.

picks.style: english winter ballad, low strings and sparse piano, grave baritone, slow, bleak, closing in
picks.why: The man lost in the snow: 'the thoughts of home / Rush on his nerves,' and night shuts round him anyway.

picks.style: english pastoral elegy, acoustic guitar and soft strings, warm tenor, unhurried, nostalgic, evening-lit
picks.why: The brook, the mill, the church on the hill, the hawthorn 'for talking age and whispering lovers made.'

picks.style: village ballad, fiddle and tabor, genial baritone, brisk, affectionate, tavern-warm
picks.why: 'And still they gaz'd, and still the wonder grew, / That one small head could carry all he knew.'

picks.style: english narrative ballad, harp and fiddle, two answering voices, plaintive, measured, candle-lit
picks.why: 'Turn, gentle Hermit of the dale' — a ballad opening that sets a whole story going in eight lines.

picks.style: javanese-sanskrit recitation, gamelan gongs and bamboo flute, measured male chant, slow, ceremonial, resonant
picks.why: Gold burned, sandalwood ground, sugarcane cut — three hammer-blows of repetition, then the wheel of joy and grief turning.

picks.style: kawi didactic chant, soft gong and drone, low even voice, steady, wry, unhurried
picks.why: A litany of the flaws of the sun, the moon, the ocean and the gods, ending: how much more so will people have flaws?

picks.style: devotional sanskrit chant, tanpura drone and small bell, warm male voice, slow, luminous, sparse
picks.why: 'The lamp of the night is the moon... in the three worlds, the lamp is dharma' — a built refrain on one image.

picks.style: greek curse song, aulos and clattering percussion, ragged gleeful chorus, fast, wild, mocking
picks.why: The poet's revenge on the cheating potters — Shatter, Smash, Charr, Crash and Crudebake summoned by name.

picks.style: greek folk begging-song, syrinx and hand drum, bright chorus of young voices, quick, festive, door-to-door
picks.why: 'I come, and I come yearly, like the swallow' — a real doorstep song, blessing and threat in the same breath.

picks.style: archaic greek epitaph chant, single lyre, clear distant voice, still, timeless, sparse
picks.why: The bronze maiden on Midas' tomb, speaking for as long as water flows and tall trees flourish.

picks.style: late latin funerary declamation, low brass drone and frame drum, sombre baritone, slow, martial, grim
picks.why: The only candidate; its core is a real tomb-epigram — the victor burying the rival he would rather have kept alive.

picks.style: greek epitaph song, lyre and soft drone, clear female voice, slow, dignified, spare
picks.why: Archedice's epitaph — daughter, sister, wife and mother of tyrants, and never once lifted up with pride.

picks.style: defiant romantic art song, piano and low strings, bold baritone, martial, rising, brief
picks.why: The only candidate, and it stands as a boast: every foeman he can see and measure with his eye.
